The hon. member for Saskatoon has conveyed an entirely wrong impression both to the house and to the public in reference to the censorship of books that pass through the customs and excise branch. We have within the department people who are capable of making translations, though not in all languages. What the hon. member has referred to had to do particularly with the time we had censorship under the Department of National War Services, of which I was minister for the last year of the war. It was not necessary nor was it economical to retain those people in the service of that department any longer, or to transfer them
Supply-Secretary of State to the Department of National Revenue, because there was not sufficient work to keep them employed full time.
When the hon. member speaks of a customs officer at a port having to take a book to a Greek restaurant proprietor in order to get a translation, that statement is entirely incorrect. It may be done, but not under the instructions of the department. Any books entering at any port of entry today, as to which there is any suspicion that they break the law because of the fact that they are immoral or obscene, are sent to headquarters in Ottawa. If they are in a foreign language they are translated here, either by translators within our own department or by translators who come under the Secretary of State. So it is not done by any haphazard method. The work is done thoroughly; and if these books break the law by reason of the fact that they are immoral or obscene, they are denied entry.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: Would I be correct in assuming that ninety per cent of these foreign language books are not examined at all?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext:
You would be entirely
incorrect.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: I am glad to hear that. Tonight, for the first time in four years, I am getting some information.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: Why did you not bring it up under the right department?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: I have brought it up under the hon. gentleman's estimates with very little success. I do know some books*-

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Liberal Party House Leader
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext:
Mr. Chairman, I
believe the discussion is taking place on the wrong item. The Minister of National Revenue just stated that the censorship of these books is in his department, and there should be some item in his estimates under which the hon. gentleman can discuss this question. The Secretary of State has said that his department does translations for other departments but that he does not know anything about censorship. So I really think the hon. gentleman should discuss this question on another occasion.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext:
I want to make just one last point, as a matter of information rather than a question. The Secretary of State did not have the information, but I can give him the figures for one particular period. At one time in the bureau of translations there were 210 translators, of whom 207 were for French and English, which left a total of three for all the other languages in the world. I do not know whether that is considered a sufficient number to examine the books that are presented for admission, but those are the facts

Supply-Secretary of State that were given to me. The only way I can find out whether or not those facts are true is to ask the minister concerned, and for having done that I offer no apology.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: I do not want the Secretary of State to think I am going after him on these estimates, because I know he is new to the department and is only following the procedure that has been laid down. My idea is to warn him that next session we will expect more details in reference to these matters. For instance, in reference to the bureau of translations, at page 255 we see that the salaries amount to $377,970. Directly below that is an item amounting to about seventy per cent of the one I have mentioned, or $251,475, as to which we have no information at all. We are simply asked to vote a blank cheque in this amount. In fairness to this committee I believe that on another occasion, in another year, we should have some explanation of this. We know this item is a wonderful vote catcher for elections, and I notice that this year it is a little larger than usual. However, we shall let that pass for the time being, though in future we shall expect to see more details given, so that we may not be asked to vote blank cheques.

Item agreed to.
407. Citizenship branch, $175,855.

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: I wonder if the Secretary of State could now give a little more information in reply to some of the questions which were asked a few moments ago. What kind of persons are employed to do this citizenship work? By that I mean what are their qualifications, and in what fields are they qualified? I think we all feel that this is a pretty important phase of governmental activity, but we would like to know what it is all about. I imagine there is a pretty good story here, if the minister could just tell it to us.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: It is mainly liaison work between the new citizens or immigrants and the provincial authorities, particularly in matters having to do with the subject of education. A great deal of the work is carried on by a voluntary organization known as the citizenship council, which as a matter of fact gets a vote of some $10,000 a year from this parliament. I cannot give much in the way of detail about it other than I have already given.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: Will the minister state the reason for the heavy increase in this particular item over last year? I believe most of it was caused by printing, stationery and office equipment. Why would it be so much greater this year than the previous year? The item shows an increase from $8,000 to $88,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext:
There is an increase of
approximately $80,000 for printing, stationery and office equipment. That is due to the cost of printing new pamphlets, the preparation of film scripts which are essential for the work of this branch, and so on. Then there was an increase in the number of radio broadcasts which accounts for the balance of the increase.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext:
How much for radio
broadcasts.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: Five thousand dollars.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: Is the minister saying that there was $80,000 more printing this year than there was last year? It seems like a fantastic increase.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: That is for printing, stationery and office equipment.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: Which is going to be the normal figure in the future, $8,000 or $88,000?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: I am afraid I cannot look far into the future, Mr. Chairman. This is a growing country.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: This item has increased ten times in one year. If it is going to increase ten times next year, I suppose it will be $880,000.

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: I believe the minister has his officials before him, and he should be able to give us some more concrete information in reply to the questions.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: Why would the printing cost increase ten times in one year? I think that is a reasonable question.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext:
I would draw to the attention of the hon. member that there were
150,000	booklets issued this year, for instance.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: What booklets would be issued this year that were not needed last year?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: I am not able to tell the hon. member at the moment.

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: Is that the end of that answer?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: That is the end.

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext:
I come back to the question I asked a moment ago. It seems to me the house is entitled to know the qualifications of the people who are doing this citizenship work. I am not asking for any names. I do not think it is fair to pull the names of civil servants out on the floor of the house, unnecessarily at any rate. In this branch, there is a director who receives $5,400; an assistant director at $4,980; a citizenship officer, grade IV at $3,600; a citizenship

officer grade II at $2,940; and a citizenship officer grade I at $2,400. What are these people-lawyers, musicians, printers or what?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: I do not think there are many expert musicians among them, Mr. Chairman. In so far as I have had association with them, I would judge them to be good citizens, well educated and with a considerable ability for organization. I do not think they do any actual teaching, so I would not regard them as teachers.

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: What do they do?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: They organize.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: Is the minister in a position to say whether anything has been done with regard to applicants for citizenship from Newfoundland? As the minister is aware, there are a number of Chinese nationals who have been living there for the past ten years and who have not been able to apply for naturalization. It is necessary for them to apply under the Canadian Citizenship Act now. Some of them are not very familiar with the English language. This particular vote provides the minister with funds to help them obtain citizenship by giving instruction in the responsibility and privileges of Canadian citizenship. I suppose nothing has been done in Newfoundland about that?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: If they have lived in Canada for twenty years they can get their citizenship papers without being able to speak the language adequately. I do not know whether or not the hon. member is referring to that.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: I believe I asked a reasonable question of the minister. Why was it necessary this year to spend eleven times more than last year for printing, stationery and office equipment? He may have answered the question, but I did not understand his answer. Was it because Newfoundland came into confederation? Was it because more immigrants came this year? Why did you have to spend eleven times more money?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext:
The hon. gentleman has asked a question which I cannot answer with the meticulous accuracy that he seems to demand, but I shall do the best I can. As I have said, there was an increase of $80,000, $70,000 of which was for printing booklets, some of which may have reached hon. members. One was called "Our Land"; another was "Our History" and still another, "Our Geography", and so on. Those were distributed in large quantities. As a matter of actual fact, I know there was a substantial 45781-141
Supply-Secretary of State quantity sent to Newfoundland and no doubt some of them went to the riding of the member for St. John's West.
An amount of $10,000 was expended for the purpose of educational film scripts. I think that accounts for the $80,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: Would you explain the purpose of those pamphlets?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: To educate those people who were coming here to be good Canadian citizens. They are newcomers to the country.

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: I have found out that the people about whom I am asking are organizers, but I should like to know what they organize. I used to be an organizer myself, but I did not get a salary like this. Of course, I was a C.C.F. organizer. I want to know what kind of organizers these fellows are who receive $3,600 and $4,980.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: They are officials of the department who are charged with the duty of endeavouring to teach newcomers to this country how to become good Canadians. One may say they are liaison officers between the immigrants and the officials, particularly the educational officials of the various provinces into which those immigrants might go. These officers try to get the two parties together. They provide educational material of various kinds for them. Those are the duties, and I believe these officials are doing a fine job.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: This is the last time I shall ask the minister about this item. It seems to me that last year there were more immigrants than this year, so why would you need $80,000 more this year.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: We are teaching them more.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: Because we have been asked for more of these educational booklets and we are doing more work.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: It would appear from the questions that have been asked during the last few minutes that there is some criticism of the increase in this item. I would suggest that the only criticism which should be made is that, instead of increasing ten times it should have increased twenty or thirty. Hon. members should know that for many years such organizations as the Daughters of the Empire have been urging that we put on something in the nature of a program of citizenship education. Now, economy is all right in its way, but I submit there is little economy in cheeseparing on the education of our new citizens.

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext:
May I say I agree one hundred per cent with what the member has

Supply-Secretary of State said. I hope that, in turn, he will agree with me that we are entitled to have this citizenship program described to us. That is all we are asking for.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: I am far from satisfied with the answers that were received from the Secretary of State.

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: What answers?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: On this particular item. The hon. member over on the other side may think that this terrific increase in that particular item is justified. He may know something about it; but the statement he has just made certainly does not give us any more information. It is no trouble to agree with him that an educational program is necessary. But why that terrific jump in one item? The minister stated that three booklets were put out last year: "Our Land," "Our History" and "Our Geography". As a member of this house I have never seen one of them.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Liberal Party House Leader
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: You are a good citizen. You do not need them.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: We should like to have a look at them. It may have been propaganda. There was an election last year. I know that when the Department of National Defence, the immigration department or any other department puts out any kind of publication, the members of the house are supplied with it. I know I have never seen one of these particular books. I should like to know why the department was hiding them or sending them out to a select group.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: I will send one over to the hon. member.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext:
I should be glad to get one. This is a terrific increase. We are not objecting to it if the minister can justify it; but he has certainly not justified it to date. I know that he is not supposed to have the answers. I do not expect him to have them. But I expect his officials who are in front of him to have the answers. In 1946, 1947 and 1948 we were bringing in to this country about the same number of immigrants as we brought in last year. I think the quota stands at about 120,000 a year. If each year up to 1949 the expenditure of that department was $8,000, why the jump to $88,000 in 1949? The minister also states that there is an item of $5,000 for radio broadcasting. I think that is quite high for that department, which is a fairly small one. An expenditure of ihat kind, without any details given, is in my opinion certainly not in order. The officials of that department should have the answers. How many of these books were sent out? I am not satisfied. I am absolutely unsatisfied
[Mr. Knowles.1
with that answer. There is something the matter with somebody when you cannot get more details than that.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: I can say this: 150,000 of these booklets were sent out and there were nine broadcasts of a half hour each across Canada.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: What was the subject of those broadcasts?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: All on citizenship.

Item agreed to.
Patent and copyright office-
409. Patent division, $488,805.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: Will the minister tell us what the reason is for the big increase in this department? There is an increase of $99,000. Will he explain the reason for that?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: That is the cost of printing patents.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext:
What does	the minister
mean?	Does he	mean	that it	costs	$99,000
more this year than last year for that?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext:
How	many	more	patents
were issued?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: Is the minister going te answer the question?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: I did not get the question. What is it?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext:
How	many	more	patents
were issued? You say this amount is for printing patents.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: It is not the number of patents that were issued. We have started printing these patents, and that was the cost of this printing.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: Formerly you did not print them?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: They were not printed before.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext:
If this large increase of $100,000, in round figures, is attributable to the printing of patents-something that was recommended two years ago by the committee on banking and commerce-there must be some offsetting revenue. I presume there will be some small revenue from the printing of these patents; it may not be all outlay.
While we are speaking of this subject of the patent and copyright office, I think the minister ought to give the committee some statement with regard to the progress the office is making in reduction of the backlog. As hon. members will recall, this has been a standing reproach for some time; it is not attributable to the present staff or to the

commissioner but to the lack of adequate personnel in times past and, up until this past year, lack of adequate accommodation. I think this committee would receive with a great deal of interest a statement from the minister indicating, now that more suitable and adequate accommodation has been provided and we hope some adequate increase in the personnel available for examination of patent applications, that some really substantial progress is being made in the reduction of that big backlog of patent applications.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: Every endeavour is being made to improve conditions. But it must be remembered that the patent office has been labouring under considerable difficulties. In the first place, the war took a good deal of the staff. In the second place, it takes some time to train staff for the patent office, particularly in the department of the examiners. Then we have to get in additional machinery to handle the ever-increasing volume of applications that are coming in to the department. We are doing the best we can. I imagine that in the near future the costs of the department are going to increase and that the revenues will increase also. Did someone ask the revenue for last year, and if there was any offset? The answer is yes, $625,450.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: What the minister has said is rather old stuff to those who were in the last house. I think the minister ought to be in a position to give us some figures about the reduction of the backlog. Surely he has some figures of the number of patent applications outstanding, we will say, two years ago, one year ago and now, which he could give to the committee, so that it will have some opportunity of satisfying itself as to whether some reduction is being made in that large backlog.

speechtext: Eleven o'clock.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: Mr. Chairman-

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: Can the minister answer the question? I asked the minister a question.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: Yes, I know; but before he answers, I have a question.

speakerposition: Deputy Chair of Committees of the Whole
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: Order. I understand the minister will now give an answer to the question asked by the hon. member for Eglinton.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: Eleven o'clock.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext:
There is a substantial backlog. The difficulty in catching up with that backlog is that, though we are getting ahead faster, we have more to handle because the number of applications is increasing con-45781-141*
Supply-Secretary of State tinually. As a matter of fact, we have to put in more linotype machines over there, and it is going to take some time for us to catch up with the backlog. But there is an ever-rolling stream coming in; that is the difficulty.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: Has the minister the figures?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: I cannot say that I have, no.

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: Eleven o'clock.

speakerposition: Deputy Chair of Committees of the Whole
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: Shall the item carry?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext: No.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE
speechtext:
Not until we get those figures.
Item stands.
Progress reported.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Liberal Party House Leader
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, tomorrow at eleven o'clock we will continue the discussion of Bill No. 144, to amend the Combines Investigation Act. We hope to conclude that in the early hours, and then take up the following bills:
Bill No. 145, respecting the acquisition of the Temiscouata railway; Bill No. 146, to authorize the granting of a subsidy to the government of the province of British Columbia in aid of the construction of an extension to the Pacific Great Eastern Railway; then another, Bill No. 12, to establish the Canadian Overseas Telecommunication Corporation; and another small bill, of only one section, Bill No. 174, to amend the Pension Fund Societies Act.
When these bills have been concluded or passed we shall take up estimates, continuing with the Department of the Secretary of State, and then proceeding to mines and resources, justice and labour.
All in one day?

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Liberal Party House Leader
speechtext: I think so.
